reasons: Direction is correct: the Company is the customer (HDI is the hosting vendor), and Section 6.1 imposes exclusivity on us for an automatically renewing term with no performance exit — a genuine high-severity deviation under EXCLUSIVITY.

The redline lands squarely on the stated fallback: exclusivity is confined to the already-defined Deerskin Products category, capped at twelve months from the Effective Date, and terminates automatically on HDI's failure to meet service level, availability or delivery date obligations.
Exclusivity that benefits us is preserved — HDI's reciprocal two-year covenant in Section 6.3 and the closeout/Joan Cook carve-outs are untouched — consistent with the redline guidance.

The failed changed-character ratio check (0.797) is explained by the necessary addition of the performance-exit sentence; no substantive language beyond the term limit and exit was rewritten, so the edit remains minimal in substance.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, states the preferred position and why the fallback is acceptable.

Minor residual risk: the cross-reference to "Sections 1.6 and 1.7" as service level/availability provisions cannot be verified from the supplied text; the drafter should confirm those citations, though the general "service level, availability or delivery date requirements of this Agreement" language makes the clause workable regardless.
